chapter: Alma Hightower and other women musicians
title: Princess Belle and other women instrumentalists
summary: Willard asks about other women in Los Angeles music; Howard names Princess Belle, who played at the Apex.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: (Recording interruption)
(inaudible) --knew that much about her.

Since she later taught different instruments, apparently, right? She taught Vi and Melba (phone crossed out) did she always know horns also? You mentioned piano and drums, but if she taught saxophone and trombone--
Piano and drums, that's what she played.
Did she also play those instruments which she taught? To the musicians we've mentioned? Later on, when she was a teacher?
I don't remember. That's why I can't remember so much because I was workin' at the--
Can you hold the mike higher?
Mr.--oh, shuh', what was--those things leave me. I can't remember. It's too much to remember.
Okay.
But, anyhow--
Were there any other women working at that same time? You mentioned on another day, a Princess Bell, who worked at the Apex, I think you said.
Yes.
And now we know about Alma Hightower.
'Cause she played down there with me, Princess Bell did.
Yeah, you told us that. Now were there any other women in Los Angeles music?
No.
Those were the only two?
(inaudible)
Huh? Yeah. I got it. Okay. Princess Bell was workin' down there. I was workin' down there, too-- (chuckle)--I was gettin' a job, hustlin' up a job, you know. I went around a hustle.
Uh-huh.

I was workin' up on top of the bandstand. So many things happened and, you know, you can't remember all those things, Buddy. Ain't no way to remember it. And nobody's gonna be able to tell 'em to you, either. And everybody's dead that had anything to do with it.
Uh-hmm.
You know. That's all there is to that.
